body:
Tested locally on Windows 11 24H2 (rebased on top of `master` https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/c6d130abd9188f313e6701d01a0ddd6ea32166a0), it mostly works as expected.

**Testing project:** [physics_interpolation_gyro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21191387/physics_interpolation_gyro.zip) (same as https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/pull/1223, but with gyro support added)
*Hold <kbd>L2</kbd> to freeze gyro so you can readjust your aim.*

Tested controllers so far:

- DualSense (wired)
- DualSense Edge (wired)

Some feedback:

- Touchpad button, touchpad finger coordinates, LED control, battery status, accelerometer and gyroscope all work.

- I couldn't get adaptive triggers to work, even when double-checking the source code to make sure I'm passing valid values. I've tried to call the method in `_ready()` (after waiting 1 frame) and `_process()` to no avail. No errors/warnings appear in the console.

- Enabling gyroscope, accelerometer and setting a light color only works if you wait 1 frame in `_ready()` using `await get_tree().process_frame`. Otherwise, the method calls seem to be ignored.

- There's no `Input.get_joy_light()` counterpart to `Input.set_joy_light()`. Does SDL provide an API for this? If implemented, it should retrieve the actual gamepad color that may have been set by another application. Otherwise, I would leave things as-is.

- `Input.set_joy_light()` should call `Color.srgb_to_linear()` on the color passed as parameter (the testing project does this in the script). This will make the color's brightness/saturation better match what you see on screen. Currently, `Color(0.2, 1, 0.2)` looks quite pastel on a DualSense Edge, while it should be a mostly saturated green.
